title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Standard for Ending Holds and Sending Hold Notices
content:
This standard governs how a hold of Hardship and Protective Holds comes to an end, the end reasons recorded, the withdrawal of an undecided request, the end-of-hold notice and the resumption of outbound contact. One clause has been retired and is carried as retired.

## 1. Ending at the end of the term

1.1 A hold ends with the end reason *term completed* only when the handling date is later than the hold's current end date counted from its start date.

1.2 *Retired — no longer in force:* "The hold's current end date is the start date plus the initial hold days plus the extension days for each extension granted, less 1, counted in calendar days." This clause is superseded by the current basis, which replaces it for every tier, and is not applied.

**Boundary.** On the current end date itself the handling date is not later than that date, so the hold does not end as term completed that day; from the day after the current end date it can.

## 2. Ending earlier, for a recorded reason

A hold also ends earlier for a recorded reason:

| End reason | When it applies |
|---|---|
| Consumer requested | The consumer asks to end the hold — always allowed where the tier lets the consumer end the hold early at any time |
| Settlement accepted | The consumer accepts a settlement on the account and the tier's hold ends on settlement acceptance |
| Dispute hold placed | A dispute places the account in dispute hold |
| Account closed | The account is paid, settled or returned |
| Assistance decided | Under the financial assistance rule |
| Service ended | A Military Service Hold's active duty has ended and the tier's post-service protection days, in calendar days, have passed |
| Documentation invalid | The documentation proves invalid and the tier ends a hold whose documentation is found invalid |

2.1 The ended date recorded is the last day the hold covered.

## 3. Withdrawal

3.1 Only the consumer can withdraw an undecided request.

## 4. Notices and resumption of contact

4.1 The end-of-hold notice is sent the tier's end-of-hold notice days, in calendar days, before the current end date.

4.2 Outbound collection contact resumes no sooner than the tier's delay before outbound contact resumes, in calendar days, after the hold ends.

4.3 Notices are sent only for a hold whose status is active or denied.

## Points of judgement

- *The consumer's spouse calls to withdraw an undecided request.* Only the consumer can withdraw an undecided request.
- *A notice for a withdrawn request.* Notices are sent only for a hold whose status is active or denied, so no notice is sent for a withdrawn request or an ended hold.
- *A hold ends early because the consumer asks.* The ended date is the last day the hold covered, and the end reason is consumer requested.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Documented Hardship Hold with a current end date of 31 July and an end-of-hold notice figure of 10 days has its end-of-hold notice sent on 21 July. On 31 July the hold has not completed its term; it can end as term completed from 1 August, with an ended date of 31 July, the last day it covered. With a resumption delay of 7 days, outbound collection contact resumes no sooner than 7 calendar days after the hold ends.
